title: Surface biotinylation of primary neurons to monitor changes in AMPA receptor surface expression in response to kainate receptor stimulation
protocol: Reduce the media in each well to 2 mL.
Transfer 500 μL of media from each well to new Eppendorf tubes.
Add 2 μL of TTX (1 mM stock).
Add 8 μL of GYKI53655 (10 mM stock).
Mix well by pipetting up and down.
Carefully add the solutions back into the respective wells, giving a final concentration in the media of 1 μM TTX and 40 μM GYKI53655.
Aspirate the drug-containing media.
Replace with prewarmed Earle’s buffer (Control and kainate).
Leave the plates in the incubator for 20 min.
Label neuronal surface proteins with Sulfo-NHS-SS-biotin for subsequent isolation using streptavidin beads.
Remove neurons from the incubator and leave on ice for 5–10 minutes.
Cooling down the neurons to 4°C prevents trafficking of the receptors.
Wash neurons with prewarmed Earle’s buffer or HBS for pharmacological stimulations.
Leave dishes containing neurons on ice for 5–10 minutes.
Aspirate the neuronal media and wash the cells twice with 2 mL of cold Earle’s buffer.
Add 1.5 mL of buffer containing 0.3 mg/mL Sulfo-NHS-SS-biotin and incubate on ice for 10 minutes, swirling gently every 2.5 minutes.
Wash the cells three times with 2 mL of cold Earle's buffer.
Aspirate the buffer and add 2 mL of 100 mM NH4Cl to each well, then incubate on ice for 1 minute.
Aspirate the buffer containing NH4Cl and gently wash once with cold Earle's buffer.
Remove the buffer and add 200 μL of neuronal lysis buffer.
Gently rotate the plate and scrape off the cells from all sides of the well using a cell scraper.
Transfer the lysate to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Sonicate the lysate briefly (3 pulses at 2.5 amplitude for ∼2 seconds).
Leave the lysate on ice for 30 minutes.
Cut the tip of the pipette for preventing damage to streptavidin beads during handling.
Add 150 μL of beads to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube containing 1 mL of wash buffer.
Centrifuge the mixture at 1500g at 4°C for 2 min and remove the supernatant by aspiration.
Repeat the washing step with another milliliter of wash buffer, centrifuge again at 1500g at 4°C for 2 min, then aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the beads in 1 mL of fresh wash buffer after the second wash.
Add 150 μL of washed beads to each of 6 Eppendorf tubes with constant inverting to ensure proper mixing.
Leave the beads on ice until the lysate is prepared (30 min–1 h).
Centrifuge the lysate at 16,000g at 4°C for 30 min to pellet cell debris.
Transfer the supernatant (the cleared lysate) to a fresh 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube without disturbing the pellet.
Add 80 μL of the cleared cell lysate to the beads.
Add 270 μL of wash buffer to each Eppendorf tube to make the final volume 500 μL (150 μL beads + 80 μL of lysate = 230 μL).
Leave the Eppendorf tube on a rotating wheel at 4°C for 1 h.
Add 20 μL of cleared cell lysate to a fresh Eppendorf tube.
Wash beads by adding 500 μL of wash buffer, centrifuging at 1500g at 4°C for 2 min, and aspirating the buffer.
Repeat the washing step two more times for a total of three washes.
Add 40 μL of 2× sample buffer to the beads after the final wash.
Add 20 μL of 2× sample buffer to the 20 μL whole lysate sample.
Heat both bead and lysate samples on a heating block at 95°C for 10 min.
Centrifuge the beads at 1500g for 2 min before loading onto an SDS-PAGE gel.
Load 20 μL of pull-down and lysate samples in separate wells for Western blotting.
